label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — resolved sink value is attacker-controlled: the user-provided header name (param) is passed through Base64 decoding and used in HTML output via encodeForHTML, but the concatenation in the response still includes the raw user input in the file path string. Alert 2 (java/path-injection): alert-TP — resolved sink value is attacker-controlled: the user-provided header name (param) is used directly in constructing the file path string, leading to path traversal vulnerability. Alert 3 (java/error-message-exposure): alert-TP — resolved sink value is attacker-controlled: error message from exception is directly printed to response without sanitization. Case TP: at least one alert-TP.

evidence.note: User-provided header name retrieved via getHeaderNames()
User input flows through Base64 decoding and used in file path construction
XSS sink: user input concatenated into HTML response
Error exposure sink: exception message printed directly to response
